topic.title: Data Structures
topic.description: Arrays, Linked Lists, Trees, Stacks, Queues, and STL Containers.

questions.title: Vector Capacity Growth
questions.explanation: Initially reserved for 2, capacity is 2. When the 3rd element is added, the vector reallocates, doubling or increasing its capacity, making capacity > 2 evaluate to true (1).

questions.title: Map Default Value
questions.explanation: Accessing m[2] using the subscript operator creates an element at key 2 with value-initialized data (which is 0 for int).

questions.title: Vector Erase Iterators
questions.explanation: Erase removes the element at v.begin() + 1 (which is 2) and returns an iterator to the next element, which is 3.

questions.title: Set Uniqueness
questions.explanation: A std::set stores unique elements and keeps them sorted.

questions.title: Array Decay
questions.explanation: In main, sizeof(a) is 40 bytes (10 * 4). When passed to the function, it decays to a pointer. sizeof(pointer) on a 64-bit system is 8 bytes.

questions.title: Priority Queue Default Ordering
questions.explanation: By default, std::priority_queue is a max-heap in C++, meaning the largest element is at the top.

questions.title: Queue FIFO
questions.explanation: A queue follows First-In-First-Out (FIFO). The first element pushed is 1, so front() returns 1. After pop(), front() returns 2.

questions.title: Stack LIFO
questions.explanation: A stack follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO). The last element pushed is 2, so top() is 2. After pop(), top() is 1.

questions.title: String Substr
questions.explanation: substr(pos, count) starts at index 1 ('e') and extracts 2 characters ('e', 'l').

questions.title: Unordered Map Order
questions.explanation: While unordered_map iteration order is not guaranteed, accessing um[1] always returns the mapped value 10 reliably.

questions.title: Vector Emplace vs Push
questions.explanation: push_back constructs a temporary X(1) (prints 'C'), then copies/moves it into the vector (prints 'L'). emplace_back constructs it directly in place, but wait! Actually, X(1) prints C. Then push_back copies it (L). Then emplace_back(2) constructs in place (C). So CLC.

questions.title: Map Insertion Operator
questions.explanation: m[1] inserts a new element with key 1 and value 0, then assigns it to 10. m[1]++ increments the value to 11. Size remains 1.

questions.title: Set Duplicate Elements
questions.explanation: Sets do not allow duplicates. The second insert fails, returning a pair where the 'second' element (a bool indicating insertion success) is false (0). Size is 1.

questions.title: Deque Iterators
questions.explanation: Unlike std::vector, inserting at the front or back of a std::deque does not invalidate pointers or references to existing elements (though it may invalidate iterators, dereferencing often still works in practice, but strictly speaking it's UB if iterators are invalidated! Wait, deque guarantees that references to elements are NOT invalidated, but iterators ARE invalidated. So using 'it' is UB).

questions.title: Priority Queue Max
questions.explanation: std::priority_queue is a max-heap by default. It returns the largest element.

questions.title: List Splice
questions.explanation: splice transfers all elements from l2 into l1. l1 size becomes 4, and l2 becomes empty (size 0).

questions.title: Unordered Map Collisions
questions.explanation: Even though all keys hash to the same bucket (collision), std::unordered_map handles collisions via chaining (linked lists) and correctly stores both distinct keys.

questions.title: String Capacity
questions.explanation: reserve(100) requests that the string capacity be at least 100 characters. It will return true (1).

questions.title: Vector Erase
questions.explanation: erase(first, last) removes elements in [first, last). It removes elements at index 1 (2) and index 2 (3). The vector becomes {1, 4}. Size is 2, index 1 is 4.

questions.title: Stack Element Order
questions.explanation: Stack is LIFO (Last In First Out). 2 is popped first, then 1.
